Christ Enthroned

Icons

Christ

Christ Enthroned

Savior on the Throne

What is depictedHistory and traditionPublished explanationSources

Scripture

Revelation 4:2–3

Revelation 19:16

King James Version · Scripture previews

Christ Enthroned depicts Christ in royal glory. Hopko’s account of the iconostasis relates the glorified Christ to his coming as King and Judge, while also identifying enthroned Christ as one traditional image behind the altar.

[1] Iconostasis paragraph; final paragraph

What is depicted

This medieval example depicts Christ seated centrally, blessing with one hand and holding a book with the other. Smaller sacred figures surround the throne and occupy the border. The file catalogue names the work Savior on the Throne, with a Selection of Saints.

[2] Displayed work; file-page title and description

History and tradition

The selected reproduction identifies the icon as a thirteenth-century work photographed at the Tretyakov Gallery. That attribution concerns the displayed example; the general subject also occurs in other centuries and church settings.

[2] File title gives thirteenth century and Tretyakov Gallery; displayed catalogue description

Published explanation

Hopko places such images within the church’s proclamation of the Kingdom. His description offers several possible altar images of Christ in glory, including enthroned, transfigured and risen representations.

[1] Final paragraph: images behind the altar

And immediately I was in the spirit: and, behold, a throne was set in heaven, and one sat on the throne. And he that sat was to look upon like a jasper and a sardine stone: and there was a rainbow round about the throne, in sight like unto an emerald.

[3] Revelation 4:2–3
